I have been having trouble with this game for a while now. Whenever I quit, I do so because I get sick and tired of the game and I just feel like it's lost its charm, its spark so to say. Whenever I have been out of the game for a while and I decide to re-sub and run some arenas to beat my peak rating, the first couple of weeks are thrilling and I really enjoy myself. I've just gotten to the point now where I've accepted the fact that I will never be able to quit this game for good and that it's only a matter of time until I return. My question to you is this: What games do you play on your downtime, whenever you don't feel like playing WoW? Are there any games comparable to the PvP aspect of WoW?
I quit WoW about five months ago, but the nostalgia keeps getting to me. What games do you play whenever you take a break from WoW to get your fix of action?

I've tried other MMOs and keep finding my way back to WoW. The thing that works best for me, though, is something completely unrelated - like writing games instead of playing them. That gets my mind off of it and I get a lot of satisfaction from actually creating something instead of consuming entertainment.

My coding experience doesn't go much further than basic Java and HTML, so that's not an option for me. But I agree, sometimes doing something that isn't even related to WoW is the best thing to get you pumped for another couple of months of active play.

I tried a private server for a brief period of time, but found it was still lacking, because what I was really missing even in the retail game was friends to play with. I've been messing around with role play in the meantime until I find something else that I have multiple friends interested in playing together.

I have to second private servers. It's been so long since most people have seen the content that it feels new and exciting again. At least in MoP, I had better experiences on private servers than on my retail account. More player interaction, more world exploring and all that.

The unfortunate side effect is that you're playing WoW without Blizz getting any compensation.

I think private servers appeal to a select few. You have people that are either nostalgic or might not have experienced the content before, have the patience to know that whatever server you join will be imperfect in addition to sharing the bugs the retail also had, and there's the legality of it all.

That being said a good number of those that pick it up are also seeking the socialization aspect that newer WoW seems to be lacking. I've found others more willing to group up, you recognize names from chat and leveling in the zone together.

I want to just take all the good things from private and all the good things from retail and mash em up into a new MMO. And I think that's what a good many folks are also looking for when they put down retail.

We need an MMO that's a "world". Not a Zombie/Crafting/Survival MMO or anything gimmicky like that. Something that sets you down, gives you a quest (to actually read instead of following a map marker) and lets you get lost while running into other players.

Too much convenience undermines what makes MMOs great: Player interaction and needing player assistance. You should have to trek across the world, get lost, coordinate with people and get phat loots on your own effort.

Coming from a background in game development, you hit the nail on the head which is nostalgia.

Sadly, you will never get that feeling back until you let go of the actual feeling you assume to remember. When we as designers make games, the idea is to bring some sort of epic journey or some character emotion in which you become one and the same. It allows you to bond to the game and feel as if you are the reason the game is the way it is. Its commonly called 'immersion'. Sadly, over the course of game development timelines, choices, scopes and other things which totally ruin what you felt (not everyone) but the reason YOU played WoW, something along the way burned the bridge of what used to be.

It could have been anything from playing with friends--having a rough time in life and you match WoW to a set emotion which fills the void. You could have had some sort of memory or emotion which bonded you to your character and then through the course of game play the elements belittled that character.

The problem isn't the game, its actually you as a player. Is a disconnection in which all gamers hit it. The moment Mario is no longer Mario but an annoying plumber which jumps on things, or a kids game. When Duke Nukem no longer is the badass of our time, but a washed up 90s action hero and cheesy to this generation. You've outgrown WoW and made new priorities. Especially true if you have been playing for 5 years. What keeps you coming back is competition it seems, which is why you mentioned playing Arena's. Human competition will always give that edge to keep pushing hard, even if you don't want to, mainly because there is always someone better than you.

So then, how do you fix it? How do you come back and play the game, or what can you do to make the game fun and useful again. The answer is. Play everything. Don't schedule anything just play naturally, set goals and do them. The problem is lack of schedule with most gamers, and that's when a game is no longer a game but a job. What do I do next, how do I come here and do this, I am overwhelmed with what to do cause there is just so much.

Stop using websites like WoWHead, MMOChampion and guides. What happens is there are no longer exploration and fun with mysteries in the game. It's sort of like how more than casual players relate LFR. Things just get handed to you. When you research or pre-hype, you kill the hype, find the shortest path, invalidate exploring and take the mystery out of the game. In another example it would be like me explaining the plot points, cut scenes and ending to the new Pixar Movie InsideOUT. It will ruin it, and you pretty much built a plan on what to expect.

I know its not the answer you were probably looking for. In fact, its probably not an answer you want to hear.

TL:DR; stop researching games, play them naturally, set goals not quotas, play everything based on moods and what you want to do. Stop doing it to just do it.
